findings.text: The site is in the Chinatown Visitor Retail (CVR) zoning district where a restaurant use on the first story is principally permitted per Planning Code § 811, effective January 14, 2024.
findings.verification_note: The records show restaurant_permission as unknown and provide no effective date of January 14, 2024.

findings.text: A 1999 Planning Department agency referral at 675 Jackson St (the same address) approved a full-service restaurant as permitted in the CVR District per Planning Code § 811.42.

Planning Code § 811 treats restaurant hours of 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. as principally permitted and 11 p.m. to 2 a.m. as conditional use; the pathway could not determine this concept's status because no closing hour was stated.
findings.verification_note: The record references § 811 but does not state the specific hour-based permission rules or explain why status could not be determined.

findings.text: Three nearby restaurant Conditional Use Authorizations in CVR and CRNC (54 m, 125 m, 127 m away) were approved with hours limited to 7 a.m.–10 p.m. or 6 a.m.–midnight.
findings.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

findings.text: Within 1,000 feet, N = 11 dated use decisions over the last 5 years show 7 approvals (1 outright, 6 with conditions) and 4 withdrawals, for a 63.6% approval rate; no denials were recorded.

findings.text: The concept describes a change from retail to restaurant use; under Planning Code § 102 definitions retail and restaurant are distinct uses, so a Planning Code change of use applies.
findings.verification_note: The record references § 102 but does not provide its definitions or state that retail and restaurant are distinct uses.

findings.text: The Building Code classifies a restaurant as Assembly Group A-2 if the occupant load is 50 or more, or Group B if fewer than 50 people; the existing occupancy group is not in public records and the concept does not state whether occupancy is above or below 50, so whether a Building Code change of occupancy is required cannot be established.

Neighborhood notification (Planning Code § 311) for a change of use was removed from the code on January 14, 2024 by Ordinance 248-23, so no § 311 notice is required for this project under the rules in force on January 21, 2024.

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pur suit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Curr ent Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation compl aints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. OPERATION (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. In additio n, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipm ent shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. Works at 415-554-.5810, http://sfdpw.org. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)

Odor Control Unit: In order to ensure any significant noxious or offensive odors are prevented from escaping the premises once the project is operational, the building permit application to implement the project shall include air cleaning or odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the plans if applicable as determined by the project planner. Odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary façade of the building. (standard)

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA, register as an employer with EDD, and secure workers' compensation insurance.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with CDTFA for the seller's permit (free, often same-day). Register with EDD within 15 days of paying wages; this is also free and online. Quote and bind workers' comp insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (restaurants typically pay 2–6% of payroll).

filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire an architect experienced in SF restaurant tenant improvements. Submit the DPH plan check application with menu, and equipment specs; specify 'health' as a routing station on the DBI application. Budget $828–$2,207 for DPH plan review (3–8 hours).

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline of 63 to 225 days and the cost of $2,170 to $18,880 are the government fees and processing times to obtain the Health Permit to Operate and the Building Permit with change of use, the two approvals in the entitlement path. These are times to approval, not to denial or withdrawal. The minimums assume straightforward plan check with no corrections and immediate scheduling of inspections; the maximums assume one round of plan corrections and rescheduled inspections. DPH plan check takes 21–60 days, building permit review and issuance 14–120 days, and construction and final inspections vary by scope (typically 30–90 days for a limited-cooking tenant improvement). Fees include: SF business registration $55–$700, DPH plan check $828–$2,207, DPH Permit to Operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (valuation-based), and state/federal registrations (EIN free, CA SOS entity $70–$150, seller's permit free). Not included: construction costs, architect and engineer fees, contractor labor, grease interceptor equipment, insurance premiums, or the sign permit ($300–$1,500 if exterior signage is installed). The 1999 site-history record and the three nearby restaurant approvals indicate that daytime restaurant use is well-established on this block; the critical path is building permit plan review and kitchen inspection readiness, not discretionary zoning review, assuming the closing hour does not extend past 11 p.m.

records_summary: The records show 675 Jackson St is in the Chinatown Visitor Retail (CVR) District where a restaurant use on the first story is principally permitted per Planning Code § 811, though the pathway rules note that hours extending beyond 11 p.m. would require conditional use review. The site history shows one 1999 Planning approval confirming restaurant use as permitted. The block is exceptionally dense with food and beverage activity: 65 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 34 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (109 within 1,000 ft), and undue concentration flagged. The nearby base rate over the last 5 years shows 7 approvals (1 outright, 6 with conditions) against 4 withdrawals and 0 denials among 11 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft—a 63.6% approval rate—indicating that restaurant projects in this CVR and adjacent CRNC area do secure approval but often with operating conditions.
data_gaps: The pathway says hours beyond 11 p.m. are conditional but could not classify this concept because no closing hour was stated; confirm intended hours to determine if a CUA is needed.
No hearing transcripts or vote tallies are available for the nearby CUA approvals, so the basis for conditions (e.g., hours limits) is not shown.
The Group Housing SUD and Priority Equity Geographies SUD overlay citations do not explain their rules; the records confirm they exist but not whether they affect this restaurant.
